kings2.23.p1.b1.text: Then the king summoned all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

kings2.23.p1.b2.text: … in their hearing he read all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

kings2.23.p1.b3.text: So the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the LORD to follow the LORD … with all his heart and all his soul, and to carry out the words of this covenant that were written in this book.

kings2.23.p1.b4.text: And all the people entered into the covenant.

kings2.23.p2.b1.text: Then the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the priests second in rank, and the doorkeepers to remove from the temple of the LORD all the articles made for Baal, Asherah, and all the host of heaven.

kings2.23.p2.b2.text: … he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.

kings2.23.p2.b3.text: … ground it to powder, and threw its dust on the graves of the common people.

kings2.23.p2.b4.text: He also tore down the quarters … in the house of the LORD, where the women had woven tapestries for Asherah.

kings2.23.p3.b1.text: … and desecrated the high places, from Geba to Beersheba, where the priests had burned incense.

kings2.23.p3.b2.text: Although the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, they ate unleavened bread with their fellow priests.

kings2.23.p3.b3.text: He also desecrated Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom so that no one could sacrifice his son or daughter in the fire to Molech.

kings2.23.p3.b4.text: And he removed … the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun. … And Josiah burned up the chariots of the sun.

kings2.23.p4.b1.text: He pulled down the altars that the kings of Judah had set up on the roof near the upper chamber of Ahaz … The king pulverized them there

kings2.23.p4.b2.text: and threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.

kings2.23.p4.b3.text: The king also desecrated the high places east of Jerusalem, to the south of the Mount of Corruption, which King Solomon of Israel had built …

kings2.23.p4.b4.text: He smashed the sacred pillars to pieces, cut down the Asherah poles, and covered the sites with human bones.

kings2.23.p5.b1.text: He even pulled down the altar at Bethel, the high place set up by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin.

kings2.23.p5.b2.text: Then he burned the high place, ground it to powder, and burned the Asherah pole.

kings2.23.p5.b3.text: And as Josiah turned, he saw the tombs there on the hillside,

kings2.23.p5.b4.text: … he sent someone to take the bones out of the tombs, and he burned them on the altar to defile it, according to the word of the LORD proclaimed by the man of God who had foretold these things.

kings2.23.p6.b2.text: “It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and pronounced these things that you have done to the altar of Bethel.”

kings2.23.p6.b3.text: “Let him rest … Do not let anyone disturb his bones.”

kings2.23.p6.b4.text: Just as Josiah had done at Bethel, so also in the cities of Samaria he removed all the shrines of the high places set up by the kings of Israel …

kings2.23.p7.b1.text: “Keep the Passover of the LORD your God, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant.”

kings2.23.p7.b2.text: No such Passover had been observed from the days of the judges who had governed Israel through all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah.

kings2.23.p7.b3.text: Furthermore, Josiah removed the mediums and spiritists, the household gods and idols, and all the abominations that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem. …

kings2.23.p7.b4.text: Neither before nor after Josiah was there any king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength, according to all the Law of Moses.

kings2.23.p8.b1.text: Nevertheless, the LORD did not turn away from the fury of His burning anger, which was kindled against Judah because of all that Manasseh had done to provoke Him to anger.

kings2.23.p8.b2.text: “… I will reject this city Jerusalem, which I chose, and the temple of which I said, ‘My Name shall be there.’”

kings2.23.p8.b3.text: … King Josiah went out to confront him, but Neco faced him and killed him at Megiddo.

kings2.23.p8.b4.text: From Megiddo his servants carried his body in a chariot, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb.

kings2.23.p9.b1.text: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months.

kings2.23.p9.b2.text: And Pharaoh Neco imprisoned Jehoahaz at Riblah in the land of Hamath … and he imposed on Judah a levy of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

kings2.23.p9.b3.text: Then Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah, and he changed Eliakim’s name to Jehoiakim.

kings2.23.p9.b4.text: … to meet Pharaoh’s demand he taxed the land and exacted the silver and the gold from the people, each according to his wealth.
